recorded: Three anyps5-retro-host processes on each system from the release workflow run 43813580226 of B-Howell/anyps5-retro-host netplay-design 67aec4e: the Windows x64 package on Windows 11 and the Linux x64 package on Ubuntu 22.04 (WSL), each running its own SwanStation 631f0fb build with the host's eight SwanStation patches (core identity anyps5-1-744335fe...c7d4) on OpenBIOS and the host's pad program (tests/make_test_disc.py pad_program), which reads both controllers, driven by a recorder built on the host repository's tests/rollback_test.py (held_script seed 7, Player, play_phase, frame_seconds) for 180 frames, as its phase without the state does but from the start: a reference in plain lockstep given every frame's input, and two players' hosts in rollback (window 8), each knowing its own port at once and the other's 1 to 6 frames late with jitter, stepping it null and correcting it when it came. Every lockstep has state false, as the launcher sends it, so no sync has a state hash. For each system, 'players' holds, for each player's host in the order the harness sent and read them, the calls, steps and corrections sent ('sent') and the welcome, replies, syncs and rollback messages the host sent ('got'), as JSON text; 'reference' holds the reference's syncs; 'tick' is the seconds a simulated frame lasted. The paths in start are left out. Windows drew with OpenGL and Linux in software.
